newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill falls to 11.70 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill falls to 11.70 pct.

text.p: The benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to an average of 11.70 percent from the week-ago 11.766 percent at Monday's regular weekly auction, the Bureau of Treasury said.
Similarly, the 182-day bill fell to an average of 12.320 from 12.424 percent; the 364-day dipped to 12.735 from 12.811 percent.
"Banks had to bid aggressively," said a dealer, by lowering their rates.
Since the government had decided not to hold next Monday's auction, banks had to have enough T-bills to service the demand of clients for two weeks, dealers said.
The Philippine government will be playing host to the November 25 summit meeting of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC).
The sale of T-bills drew 8.085 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which 3.5 billion pesos were accepted.
